entry.title: Re: Fiori Elements OData V2: Incorrect object-page header...
entry.content:
Hello,

Thank you very much for your question. Here's the AI-generated response. Please check whether it helps you resolve the issue.

Kind regards,

Henrike

Joule Response

Troubleshooting: Fiori Elements Object-Page Header & Navigation Hierarchy in RAP Composition

The slash-separated header values you are seeing (e.g., 8001 / on Customer Address and 8001 / / on Tax) are a classic symptom of Fiori Elements being unable to resolve the title or description annotation for one or more levels in the composition hierarchy. Fiori Elements for OData V2 builds the breadcrumb/header by traversing the composition chain upward and reading the @UI.headerInfo annotation at each level. When a level returns an empty or unresolved value, it renders as a blank segment — hence the trailing slashes.

Below is a structured diagnostic and resolution guide covering all three layers you asked about.

Possible Causes

  1. Missing or incorrect @UI.headerInfo annotations in one or more projection views — the most common root cause of blank slash segments.
  2. Parent association not correctly exposed or redirected in the projection view or projection behavior definition, preventing upward navigation context resolution.
  3. Composition or $self join condition mismatch across hierarchy levels, causing the framework to fail silently when resolving parent keys.
  4. OData V2 navigation property binding incomplete for nested entities beyond two levels deep, which is a known consideration for deeper composition trees. [1]

How Fiori Elements Resolves the Slash-Separated Header

In a RAP-based Fiori Elements OData V2 application, the object-page header breadcrumb is constructed as follows:

  • For each object page in the navigation stack, Fiori Elements reads the @UI.headerInfo.title.value (and optionally @UI.headerInfo.description.value) from the projection view of that entity.
  • It then traverses the parent association (association to parent) upward through the composition tree to obtain the parent's title for the breadcrumb prefix.
  • The slash separator is inserted between each resolved level.

If @UI.headerInfo.title.value points to a field that is null, empty, or not exposed in the projection view, that segment renders as blank — producing the 8001 / or 8001 / / pattern you observe. [2]

The depth of your hierarchy (Customer → Company Code → Tax = 3 levels) is supported by the framework — more than 3 levels are explicitly supported in RAP Fiori Elements. [1]

Resolution Steps

Step 1 — Verify @UI.headerInfo on Every Projection View

Check each projection view entity in your hierarchy. Every entity that has its own object page must declare:

 
@UI.headerInfo: {
  typeName: 'Customer Address',
  typeNamePlural: 'Customer Addresses',
  title: {
    type: #STANDARD,
    value: 'AddressID'          -- must be a non-null, exposed field
  },
  description: {
    type: #STANDARD,
    value: 'Street'             -- optional but recommended
  }
}

Critical checks:

  • The field referenced in title.value must be selected and exposed in the projection view — not just in the base/interface view.
  • For UUID-keyed entities, do not use the raw UUID as the title value unless you have a semantic label field. If no meaningful label exists, use a concatenated or virtual element.
  • For the Tax entity (child of Company Code, which is child of Customer), the header shows 8001 / / — meaning two levels above Tax are failing to resolve. Check both the Tax projection view and the Company Code projection view for missing @UI.headerInfo.title.value fields.
Step 2 — Check Parent Association Exposure in Projection Views

In each child projection view, the association to parent must be redirected to the corresponding consumption/projection view:

 
-- In the Customer Address projection view (ZC_CustomerAddress):
define view entity ZC_CustomerAddress
  as projection on ZI_CustomerAddress
{
  key CustomerAddressUUID,
  CustomerUUID,
  Street,
  City,
  -- ...
  /* Associations */
  _Customer : redirected to parent ZC_Customer   -- MUST be present
}

If _Customer is not redirected to the projection-layer parent (ZC_Customer), Fiori Elements cannot traverse upward to resolve the parent's title for the breadcrumb. [3] [4] [5]

For the Tax entity (two levels deep under Customer), the chain must be complete:

  • Tax projection → _CompanyCode : redirected to parent ZC_CompanyCode
  • Company Code projection → _Customer : redirected to parent ZC_Customer

A break at any level in this chain causes blank segments in the header.

Step 3 — Validate Composition and Association Definitions in Behavior Definitions

In the projection behavior definition, verify that the parent association is exposed for each child entity:

 
projection;

define behavior for ZC_Customer alias Customer
{
  use create;
  use update;
  use delete;

  use association _CustomerRole { create; }
  use association _CustomerAddress { create; }
  use association _CompanyCode { create; }
}

define behavior for ZC_CustomerAddress alias CustomerAddress
{
  use update;
  use delete;

  use association _Customer;   -- parent association must be declared here
}

define behavior for ZC_CompanyCode alias CompanyCode
{
  use update;
  use delete;

  use association _Customer;   -- parent association
  use association _Tax { create; }
}

define behavior for ZC_Tax alias Tax
{
  use update;
  use delete;

  use association _CompanyCode;  -- parent association
}

If the parent association is not declared with use association in the projection behavior definition, the OData V2 service will not generate the corresponding navigation property, and Fiori Elements cannot resolve the upward navigation context. [3] [4]

Step 4 — Inspect the OData V2 Service Binding

After correcting annotations and behavior definitions, re-activate the service binding and verify in the service preview:

  • Each entity set must have navigation properties pointing to its parent entity set.
  • For Tax (two levels deep), you should see navigation properties: _CompanyCode on the Tax entity set, and _Customer on the Company Code entity set.
  • If navigation properties are missing, the root cause is typically the missing use association _Parent in the projection behavior definition (Step 3).

For OData V2 specifically, navigation property resolution for nested entities beyond two levels requires that every intermediate association is correctly exposed — there is no automatic inference across skipped levels. [6] [7]

Key Annotation & Definition Checks

Layer What to Check Expected Behavior
CDS Projection View@UI.headerInfo.title.value on every entity with an object pageDisplays a meaningful, non-null label per entity in the breadcrumb
CDS Projection View_Parent : redirected to parent ZC_<ParentEntity>Enables upward navigation context resolution
Projection Behavior Definitionuse association _Parent; declared for each child entityOData V2 generates the navigation property for parent traversal
Interface (Base) Viewassociation to parent ZI_<ParentEntity> as _Parent on $projection.<ParentUUID> = _Parent.<ParentUUID>Correct join condition — UUID field names must match exactly
Service DefinitionAll entities (Customer, CustomerRole, CustomerAddress, CompanyCode, Tax) explicitly listedAll entity sets and navigation properties are generated in the OData metadata
OData V2 BindingNavigation properties visible in service preview for each child→parent directionHeader resolves parent key and title correctly at each level

Summary of the Most Likely Root Cause for Your Specific Pattern

Observed Header Most Likely Missing Element
8001 / on Customer Address@UI.headerInfo.title.value on the Customer Address projection view is missing or points to a null/unexposed field
8001 / / on Tax@UI.headerInfo.title.value missing on both Company Code and Tax projection views, or the parent association chain is broken at the Company Code → Customer level

Start by auditing the @UI.headerInfo annotation on the Company Code and Tax projection views first, then verify the _Parent association redirect and use association _Parent in the projection behavior definition for those two entities. [2]

  • [2] Fiori Elements OData V2: Incorrect object-page header and navigation hierarchy in a nested RAP BOSAP Community
  • [3] Developer Guide: From Classic ABAP to ABAP CloudSAP Help
  • [4] Defining the Business Object Structure for a BAPI-Based RAP BO | SAP Help PortalSAP Help

  • [6] RAP / Restful Application Programming Mode: ListReport on ObjectPage but restrict further navigationSAP Community

entry.title: SAP Table to CDS Mapper - New Version thanks to AI-supported Development
entry.content:
TL;DR

I created a standalone HTML analysis that helps developers find possible CDS objects from a standard SAP table or table field. It combines direct field lineage with official successor hints and Cloudification Repository C1-release evidence. The snapshot covers 121,303 successfully analyzed CDS objects, 20,028 physical tables, and 1,647,510 direct field mappings and showed promising successors for over 2,000 tables that have no official successor at the moment.

Download the analysis package (ZIP). Extract it and open the HTML file; no SAP-system installation or additional service is required.
**This is a discovery accelerator, not an SAP replacement decision. The developer must validate business scope, semantics, authorizations, and performance for the intended use case.**

What is the issue here?

Finding a possible CDS object for a familiar SAP table is still more difficult than it should be. The Cloudification Repository, released object trees in ADT, and the SAP Business Accelerator Hub are valuable starting points. But successor information is not available for every table, and developers often start with a table and a field rather than the business-object vocabulary needed to find the right CDS object.

In my earlier post, How to find a CDS view for a classic Table in ABAP - Cheat Sheet, I described a pragmatic way to reverse-engineer direct table-to-CDS field relationships. This post takes the same idea one step further: I ran the analysis broadly on an SAP S/4HANA 2025 FPS01 system and created a portable report that lets a developer start from a standard table or a table field.

Important disclaimer: This is not an SAP tool and it is not a replacement-decision engine. It is an accelerator for discovering candidate CDS objects. A structural field mapping, a C1-release indicator, or even an official-successor indication does not prove semantic, functional, authorization, cardinality, filtering, or performance equivalence. The developer still has to validate that a candidate fits the concrete requirement.

Why an additional mapping is useful

The usual SAP tools rely heavily on maintained successor information. That is the strongest signal where it exists. However, not every classic table has a maintained successor. And an object can map relevant fields without being listed as a formal successor.

One useful example is T001L, the storage-location table. In the analyzed snapshot, it has no official-successor entry. Nevertheless, the report identifies I_StorageLocation as a C1-released candidate with direct mappings for 9 of the 22 persisted table fields. This is not a statement that I_StorageLocation replaces every T001L use case. It is a concrete, inspectable starting point for a developer who otherwise might not know where to look.

Using a deliberately cautious rule (no explicit official successor, a C1-release signal, at least three directly mapped fields, at least 30% direct coverage, excluding CUBE and value help views) the snapshot identifies 2,071 DB tables with a C1 released view as starting point. The Table explorer marks these as Good C1 candidate available and can filter for them. This is a prioritization signal only: it does not make the candidate an official successor or guarantee that it is suitable for a specific requirement.

For teams using Project Kernseife, I also provide a BF5 External classification import for these 2,071 additional successors. Choose not to overwrite existing classifications if you want to leave any existing custom classification untouched; those existing records will not be replaced by this import. If you choose overwrite instead, review the complete classification and preserve any existing successors that must remain. The classification is still only a curated discovery aid: validate that each CDS candidate fits the required business scope and works for the intended use case before relying on it.

What was analyzed

The snapshot was compiled in October 2026 on SAP S/4HANA 2025 FPS01. It contains metadata only; no business data was read or exported.

  • 130,647 CDS entities were placed in the extraction queue.
  • 121,303 CDS entities were analyzed successfully.
  • 20,028 physical base tables have persisted field-denominator metadata in the local report.
  • 1,647,510 non-calculated direct field-mapping rows are available for analysis.

* Not every available CDS object could be analyzed. This does not remove the value of the evidence that is present, but it means the report must not be interpreted as a complete catalog or a replacement decision.

How the data is compiled

The technical core is SAP class CL_DD_DDL_FIELD_TRACKER. For each analyzed CDS definition, it provides base-field information. The extractor keeps direct relationships between a CDS element and an underlying table field. Calculated elements are retained separately where useful, but they do not increase direct field coverage.

The process is broadly:

  1. Discover relevant standard CDS definitions in the analyzed system.
  2. Read direct CDS-element-to-base-table-field lineage.
  3. Persist physical-table field metadata so coverage can be calculated.
  4. Enrich CDS candidates with effective release, C1/cloud-usage, and official-successor evidence when the system provides it.
  5. Reverse the result: table and table field to candidate CDS entities and elements.
  6. Rank candidates: official successor first, then C1-released candidates, then direct field coverage.

I am especially grateful to Andreas Graeber. He shared the idea and solution with me before he open sourced and published CDS Analyser. Publishing it gave the community a practical implementation to inspect, reuse, and improve. This analysis builds on that generous contribution.

As mentioned in the title - this was done leveraging a new AI harness, so I tried "Hermes" for the first time (and quite liked it). I admit, it is mainly vibe-coded, so if you have ideas on how to improve this, feel free to take it from here!

How to use the report

The report has three views:

  • Use and limitations explains the purpose, evidence model, and validation boundary.
  • Table explorer lets a developer search a table, inspect the ranked candidate CDS objects, filter for official successors, C1-released candidates, or the cautious good-candidate signal, and expand a candidate to see the direct field mappings.
  • Overview provides aggregate coverage and concentration statistics for the snapshot.

You can identify possible successors in the Table explorer as shown in this example for T001L, which indicates I_StorageLocation as C1-released view that is worth diving into:

 

The field filter is especially useful for focused questions. For example, a developer can select EKKO, enter STCEG, and see only CDS candidates with a direct mapping for that field. The same filter updates field coverage. Candidate filters also update coverage: if the developer selects only C1-released candidates, fields that are not mapped by any C1 candidate are shown as gaps.

Evidence, not a guarantee

This distinction matters. A CDS object can deliberately model only part of a table's scope. The well-known repository-directory example of TADIR is useful here: a CDS object like the successor I_CUSTABAPOBJDIRECTORYENTRY may expose customer-created repository objects while intentionally excluding standard objects. A high mapping percentage can therefore still be wrong for a particular consumer.

For that reason, the report makes the evidence visible instead of turning it into a binary recommendation:

  • Official successor means that the system provides explicit successor evidence.
  • C1 released means that the snapshot found C1-release evidence for ABAP Cloud usage.
  • Coverage means direct structural field mapping, not business equivalence.
  • Good C1 candidate available is a cautious discovery filter for tables without official successor evidence; it is neither an SAP endorsement nor a replacement guarantee.
  • Unreleased candidates remain visible for investigation but are not presented as released API recommendations.

This aligns with the broader Clean Core principle: release information is important guidance, but developers still need to understand the intended API and validate that it meets their use case. The mapping helps to reduce the time spent searching; it does not remove engineering judgment.

Where this can help next

I see this primarily as a discovery aid for modernization work, custom-code remediation, and development teams that are moving away from direct table access. It can also support project-specific governance: once a team has validated suitable CDS objects for its relevant scenarios, those decisions can be maintained as explicit project rules rather than rediscovered repeatedly.

The result is provided as a standalone HTML analysis. Like the Excel sheet in the earlier post, it can be opened and used directly without installing anything in an SAP system or running an additional service. Refreshing the analysis for a later Feature Package Stack is still necessary, because available CDS content and release status can change.

If you use this kind of mapping, I would be interested in hearing which evidence you find most useful: official successors, C1 release, direct coverage, field-level lookup, or additional factors such as key fields and business-object metadata.

References

  • How to find a CDS view for a classic Table in ABAP - Cheat Sheet
  • agraeber/cdsanalyser
  • Cloudification Repository Viewer
  • Project Kernseife

entry.content:
Hello,

Thank you very much for your question. 

Here's the AI-generated response. Please check whether it helps you resolve the issue.

Kind regards,

Henrike

Troubleshooting: Stock Not Transferred After Usage Decision in Inspection Lot

This is a known scenario in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. The root cause and the standard correction procedure are well-documented in SAP KBAs and Help Portal content.

Possible Causes

  1. UD code not configured for automatic stock posting: The Usage Decision code used may not have a movement type assigned for automatic background stock posting. If the UD code is configured without a posting proposal or background flag, the stock remains in Quality Inspection stock after the UD is saved, requiring a manual stock posting step that may have been missed. [1]

  2. Stock posting was not completed during the UD transaction: It is possible to record a Usage Decision (entering the UD code and saving) without completing the stock posting step. These are two separate system actions — the UD status (system status UD) and the stock posting status (SPCO — Stock Posting Completed) are tracked independently. If the stock posting was not performed at the time of the UD, the quantity remains in Quality Inspection stock. [2]

Resolution Steps

Since the Usage Decision has already been recorded and you are unable to modify it directly, the standard SAP correction procedure in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition involves the following two-step approach:

Step 1 — Reset the Usage Decision

  • Log on to the SAP Fiori Launchpad as a Quality Engineer.
  • Open the Manage Usage Decisions app (Fiori ID: F2345).
  • Navigate to the Usage Decision object page for the affected inspection lot.
  • Choose Reset Usage Decision and confirm with OK. [3]
  • The inspection lot system status will change from UD to UDRE, and the UD code and quality score will be initialized (cleared). [4]

Important Prerequisites for the Reset button to be visible:

  • The business catalog SAP_QM_BC_USAGE_DCSN_EXTD_PC must be assigned to the user. [3]
  • The Reset UD checkbox must be enabled for the relevant inspection type at plant level via configuration: Maintain Settings at Plant Level (SSCUI 102456). [5]
  • If the Reset Usage Decision button is not visible, verify both prerequisites above.

Critical Note: Resetting the Usage Decision does not reverse any stock postings that were already made. It only resets the UD status. Since in your case the stock was not transferred (i.e., no stock posting was made), this step clears the UD so you can re-record it correctly. [3] [4]

Step 2 — Re-record the Usage Decision with the Correct Stock Posting

After the reset (status is now UDRE), re-record the Usage Decision with the appropriate UD code that triggers the stock transfer to Unrestricted-Use stock:

  • In the Manage Usage Decisions app (F2345), open the inspection lot.
  • Select the appropriate UD code (e.g., A1 – Accepted – Unrestricted Stock). [6]
  • In the Inspection Lot Stock section, verify the quantity to be posted to Unrestricted-Use stock.
  • Choose Save. The system will automatically trigger the goods movement from Quality Inspection stock to Unrestricted-Use stock. [6]
Additional Scenario: If Stock Was Already Partially Moved or the Situation Is More Complex

If the stock posting was partially executed or the situation involves a previously incorrect UD with stock already moved, the correction requires an additional step using movement type 322:

  • After resetting the UD (Step 1 above), use the Transfer Stock – In-Plant app (Fiori ID: F1061) to post the stock back from Unrestricted-Use stock into Quality Inspection stock using movement type 322. [7] [8]
  • Prerequisite: Inspection type "Stock Transfer" (origin 08) must be activated in the product master's Quality Management view.
  • Once the stock is back in Quality Inspection, it will be managed under a new inspection lot number. Re-record the Usage Decision on the new inspection lot. [9] [10]
Summary Table
Situation Action Required
UD recorded, no stock posting made, cannot modify UDReset UD (F2345) → Re-record UD with correct stock posting
UD recorded, stock already moved incorrectlyReset UD (F2345) → Use F1061 (MT 322) to move stock back → Re-record UD on new inspection lot
Reset UD button not visibleAssign business catalog SAP_QM_BC_USAGE_DCSN_EXTD_PC + enable Reset UD in SSCUI 102456

For further reference, the following SAP Notes are directly relevant to this scenario:

  • SAP KBA 3359470 – Reset Usage Decision does not reverse stock postings (standard behavior) [4]
  • SAP Note 2695182 – Reversal of goods movements after usage decision (movement type 322 workaround) [7]
  • SAP KBA 3022268 – How to reset usage decision and reverse its stock postings (comprehensive guide) [2]

entry.title: Re: QM UD REVERSAL FIORI APP
entry.content:
The reset in Manage Usage Decisions takes back only the decision. It does not touch the stock posting, and that is by design: after the reset the lot has nothing left that it could post again. To correct the stock, I would reverse the material document that the UD posted and then make the UD again (I did not run that reversal, see the end). I measured the status rules and the code on an S/4HANA 2023 system and ran the reset in check mode on a lot whose UD had posted the full quantity to unrestricted use.

What I measured

  • The reset action of the inspection lot runs function module QEVC_RESET_UD. Its result has one lot field, the UD flag (QALS-STAT35), and the fields of the decision record (code group, code, valuation, quality score, follow up action). In its code the only lot fields it changes are STAT35 and STAT14, so the posted quantities, the quantity still to be posted and the linked material documents stay as they are.
  • Field RESET_UD_ALLOWED of table TQSS1_AVE (per plant and inspection type) allows the reset, and its documentation says that stock postings are not revoked.
  • Revoke usage decision (business transaction QM68) in table TJ06: sets REL and UDRE, removes UD, STIC and ICCO. It does not remove SPCO "Stock posting completed".
  • Stock posting after the UD (QM38 "Start inv. pstg after UsageDec") is prohibited by REL in table TJ07. Field QALS-LMENGEZUB is documented as "the quantity of the inspection lot that must still be posted to stock", and it is 0 once the UD has posted everything.
  • Table QAMB links the lot to its material documents. Type 3 is "Material Documents for a Usage Decision Transfer Posting" and type 7 is "Canceled Material Docs for Usage Decision Transfer Posting".

What I ran (check mode only, rolled back, nothing saved)

  • A lot whose UD posted all of it to unrestricted use: SPCO active, quantity posted to unrestricted equal to the lot quantity, quantity still to be posted 0, one QAMB link of type 3 with stock type "To Unrestricted Use".
  • QM38 on that lot: allowed. QEVC_RESET_UD in check mode: passed, and returned the lot without the UD flag and without the UD code.
  • QM68 applied only in memory: UD, STIC and ICCO gone, REL and UDRE active, SPCO still active. QM38 again: refused with BS 013 for status REL.

What I would do: take the material document of the UD posting (the QAMB link of type 3 for your lot), reverse it with MBST "Cancel Material Document", check that the stock is back in quality inspection stock and that the lot shows a quantity to be posted again, then make the UD and post the right stock type. If you think of reversing the goods receipt instead: the QM function for cancelling the document that created the lot raises QA 082 and QA 083 "Material doc. cancellation not possible since insp. stock transferred".

What I did not test: the reversal itself (it would post in my system), so I cannot show you that the lot gets the quantity back; the screens of both apps; and what Transfer Stock posts. The tables, texts, code and the check runs above are measured.

Auto-Population of Settlement Rules: WBS (Sender) → GL (Receiver)
Current Findings

  • CJB1 Strategy Determination Gap for GL Receiver: The standard strategy determination for automatic settlement rule generation (CJB1/CJB2) in SAP S/4HANA supports the following account assignment categories: settlement to profitability segment, settlement to responsible cost center, settlement to requesting cost center, take over settlement rule from superior object, and no settlement rule. A dedicated strategy for GL account as receiver is not available in the standard configuration.

  • Enhancement Point Investigation: The BAdI WBS_SETTLEMENT_RULE exists to influence the generation of settlement rules for WBS elements in transactions CJB1 and CJB2. It provides the method DETERMINE_STRATEGY, which allows custom strategy determination using project definition and WBS element parameters. However, in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, the ability to create active BAdI implementations via custom ABAP enhancements is restricted compared to on-premise. [1] [2]

Root Cause Analysis

  • Why GL Receiver Strategy is Unavailable in Standard CJB1: The standard strategy determination for WBS settlement rules is designed around CO-relevant receiver types (cost center, profitability segment, superior WBS). GL account as a standalone receiver type is not delivered as a strategy option in the standard customizing path (SPRO → Project System → Costs → Automatic and Periodic Allocations → Settlement → Settlement Rule for Work Breakdown Structure Element → Determine Strategy for Settlement Rule). [2]

  • Settlement Profile Constraint for GL Receiver: For a GL account to be used as a settlement receiver at all, the settlement profile must explicitly allow it. In S/4HANA releases, enhanced checks validate settlement rules with GL account receivers against the settlement profile — if the receiver type is set to "Settlement Not Allowed," error KD132 is triggered. The GL account receiver type must be set to "Settlement Optional" in transaction OKO7 (SSCUI: SIMG_CFMENUORKKOKO7). [3]

  • Revenue Projects Restriction: For revenue-carrying WBS elements (revenue projects), settlement to a GL account (e.g., a sales account) is not supported. Revenue projects must not be settled; the only available settlement category in that context is profitability segment (PSG). [4]

  • Public Edition vs. On-Premise Limitations: In S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, project profiles are delivered via pre-delivered content and cannot be configured by customers. Project profiles determine the settlement profile, which in turn controls allowed receiver types. Additionally, the mass API/CDS view for settlement rules on WBS elements is not available in Public Edition. [5] [6]

Recommended Approach

1. Enable GL as Allowed Receiver in the Settlement Profile

  • Navigate to OKO7 (or the equivalent SSCUI in Public Edition) and set the GL account receiver type to "Settlement Optional" rather than "Settlement Not Allowed" in the relevant settlement profile. This is a prerequisite before any GL-based settlement rule can be created or auto-populated. [3]

2. Source Structure Configuration for Differentiated Settlement

  • Define a source structure that groups debit cost elements on the WBS sender according to the same distribution rule. For example:
    • Source Assignment 1: Primary cost elements → settle to GL Receiver A
    • Source Assignment 2: Secondary cost elements → settle to GL Receiver B (or split %)
  • Once the source structure is defined, use the source assignments in the distribution rules to map different settlement receivers per source. This is the standard mechanism for routing different cost types to different receivers. [5]
  • The source structure is configured in the allocation structure/settlement profile area and referenced in the settlement rules of the WBS element.

3. BAdI WBS_SETTLEMENT_RULE for Custom Strategy Determination

  • The BAdI WBS_SETTLEMENT_RULE (method: DETERMINE_STRATEGY) can be used to implement custom logic for strategy determination during CJB1/CJB2 execution. This BAdI allows you to return a custom strategy (E_STRAT) based on project definition and WBS element attributes. [1] [2]
  • Important: In S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, the availability of custom BAdI implementations is subject to the extensibility framework (SAP BTP Side-by-Side or in-app extensibility). You should verify whether this specific BAdI is exposed as a released extensibility point in your Public Edition tenant before planning this approach.
  • If the BAdI is not available as a released extension point in Public Edition, the alternative is to manually maintain settlement rules via the "Manage Settlement Rules" Fiori apps, or raise a Feature Request via SAP Influence (https://influence.sap.com/sap/ino/#/) to request GL receiver strategy support in CJB1. [6]

4. Manual or Semi-Automated Rule Maintenance

  • For mass maintenance scenarios, the "Generate Settlement Rules – Projects" app (CJB1) currently supports overhead projects (→ responsible cost center) and investment projects (→ AuC pass-down). For GL receiver scenarios not covered by standard strategies, settlement rules must be maintained manually in the WBS master data or via the Manage Settlement Rules apps. [7] [8]
Key Constraints
Constraint Detail
Public Edition project profile restrictionProject profiles are pre-delivered; customers cannot configure them. They determine the settlement profile. [5]
Supported auto-generation receiver typesStandard CJB1 strategies support: responsible cost center, requesting cost center, profitability segment, superior WBS, no settlement. GL account is not a standard strategy receiver type. [9]
Mass API unavailabilityNo API/CDS view exists for mass settlement rule creation on WBS in Public Edition. [6]
Revenue project restrictionWBS elements carrying revenue must not be settled; GL account settlement to sales accounts is not supported for revenue projects. [4]
Settlement profile prerequisiteGL account receiver must be set to "Settlement Optional" in OKO7/settlement profile before any GL-based rule can be created. [3]
BAdI extensibility

BAdI WBS_SETTLEMENT_RULE exists on-premise; availability as a released extension point in Public Edition must be confirmed in your tenant. [1] [2]

entry.title: Re: Error in a service of application MMPUR Function not...
entry.content: Root cause from SAP: Specifically: - The CLID had been updated to version 8 through multiple amendments - However, ExternalPublishVersion was still set to 4, meaning Ariba believed ECC had last received version 4 - When Ariba attempted to send the CLID to ECC via the PurchasingContractERPRequest_In_V1 service, ECC's MMPUR module evaluated the incoming request against its current contract state and rejected it with "Function not possible for a contract" because the version gap made the operation invalid from ECC's perspective Why does this happen? The ExternalPublishVersion is updated automatically each time a successful sync completes between Ariba and ECC. If any prior send attempt fails or is interrupted without ECC acknowledging receipt, ExternalPublishVersion does not advance — it stays at the last successfully acknowledged version. Over time, as the contract is amended in Ariba, the gap between the current CLID version and ExternalPublishVersion grows, eventually causing ECC to reject subsequent sends.

Hello @Patrcia_Teixeira 

TL/DR: Don't do it. It'll bring MRP to its knees.

MDUM is supposed to convert planned orders to production orders that you are going to actually execute (produce). I'm pretty sure you can't reliably tell what you are going to produce in 7000 years.

MRP can create, reschedule and delete planned element, i.e. purchase requisitions and planned orders. Once they are converted to scheduled elements, i.e. purchase orders and production orders, they can't be changed by MRP anymore. If a change to scheduled elements is required, MRP issues an exception. Exceptions must be dealt with by MRP controllers. 

Therefore, if you convert all your planned orders in production orders with MDUM for year 9999, your supply plan will get fixed and it won't be automatically adjusted by MRP anymore. You will get a barrage of MRP exceptions instead.

I wonder who came up with this crazy idea and why.

Implementation Approach

The recommended approach leverages the Form Template Extensibility and BAdI (Business Add-In) capabilities available in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition for Account Statement correspondence. [1] [2]

Key Technical Objects:

  • Form Name: FIN_FO_CORR_ACC_STAT
  • OData Service: FDP_FFO_CORR_ACC_STAT_SRV

  • BAdI Extension Point: ACCST_ADJUST_DATA_BEFORE_RNDR — BAdI: Adjustment of Data in Account Statement Before Rendering [1]
  • App: Custom Logic (App ID: F6957)

Step 1 – Copy the Standard Account Statement Form Template

  • Open the Maintain Form Templates app (App ID: F1434).
  • Search for the standard Account Statement form template (FIN_FO_CORR_ACC_STAT).
  • Download the existing form template. [1] [2]

Step 2 – Modify the Form Template (Adobe LiveCycle Designer)

  • Open the downloaded XDP file in Adobe LiveCycle Designer.
  • Add a new section/fragment at the end of the form to display:
    • Debit Total (right-aligned, clearly labelled)
    • Credit Total (right-aligned, clearly labelled)
    • Difference Amount (Debit Total – Credit Total)
  • Ensure the new section is visually distinct and does not overlap or modify the existing Account Statement layout. [2]
  • Upload the modified template as a Custom Form Template in the Maintain Form Templates app. [1]

Step 3 – Implement the BAdI for Data Aggregation

  • Open the Custom Logic app (App ID: F6957).
  • Create a new Enhancement Implementation using the following extension point:
    • Extension Point ID: ACCST_ADJUST_DATA_BEFORE_RNDR
    • Extension Point Description: BAdI: Adjustment of Data in Account Statement Before Rendering [1]
  • In the BAdI implementation, write logic to:
    • Iterate over the line items in the account statement data.
    • Aggregate Debit amounts (where Debit/Credit Indicator = S) separately.
    • Aggregate Credit amounts (where Debit/Credit Indicator = H) separately.
    • Calculate the Difference Amount (Debit Total – Credit Total).

Note: The Debit/Credit Indicator field (DRCRK) uses S for Debit and H for Credit in the Universal Journal. [3]

Step 4 – Configure Output Parameter Determination

Step 5 – Assign the Custom Form Template

  • Navigate to Manage Your Solution / Central Business Configuration.
  • Select Assign Form Templates (ID: 102313) and assign the new custom template as the Account Statement form. [1]

Step 6 – Test and Validate

  • Verify in the PDF output:
    • Existing Account Statement data and layout are unchanged.

Warehouse Management Capabilities: 3BR & 3BS Scope Items

Yes / No + Clarification

Yes — with important context. Activating scope items 3BR (Warehouse Inbound Processing) and 3BS (Warehouse Outbound Processing) in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition is sufficient to manage warehouse stock at the storage type and storage bin levels, including stock quantity tracking, putaway, and picking. No separate EWM license or additional "Advanced Warehouse Management" license is required. [1] [2]

Warehouse Management in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition is technically based on the SAP EWM engine, but it is standardized and tailored to a clearly defined, low-maintenance scope of functions for the public cloud. It is not a separate product — it is embedded EWM delivered as part of the standard S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition license. [3]

When 3BR and 3BS are activated, the following core capabilities become available: [4] [5]

  • Storage bin-level stock management — including creation and management of storage bins, storage types, and warehouse structure [6]
  • Putaway (Inbound) — warehouse tasks for putaway with bin search strategies (fixed bin, free space search, bulk storage) are supported under 3BR [4] [3]
  • Picking (Outbound) — warehouse tasks for picking, packing, and staging are supported under 3BS [5]
  • Stock quantity tracking — the Warehousing – Stock Integration API (SAP_COM_0755) becomes available when either 3BR or 3BS is activated, enabling retrieval of available and physical stock in the warehouse [7]
  • Master data integration (SAP_COM_0374) — provides OData services for Warehouse, Warehouse Storage Type, Warehouse Storage Bin, and Fixed Bin Assignment, activated by 3BR

One important operational note: if the delivery is EWM-relevant, an inbound delivery is mandatory to perform goods receipt with a warehouse task. Direct GR without an inbound delivery is not the standard path for EWM-managed stock. [8]

Additionally, the warehouse management scope items in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition are non-standard scope items — they are not activated by default and must be explicitly included in your solution scope. The activation is performed on the SAP side; you can request it by submitting a ticket to SAP for component XX-S4C-OPR-SRV. [1] [9]

Additional Requirements (if applicable)

3BR and 3BS cover the core inbound/outbound bin-level processes. However, depending on your business requirements, you may wish to consider the following complementary (not mandatory) scope items: [2]

Scope Item Capability Added
3BX – Warehouse Physical InventoryBin-level physical inventory counting
3BU – Warehouse Posting ChangesStock type changes at bin level
3BT – Warehouse Ad Hoc Goods IssueAd hoc stock movements
3BW – Warehouse Internal RepackingInternal repacking processes
3DV – Warehouse Production IntegrationProduction supply and goods receipt from production
3W0 – Resource Management in WarehousingMobile warehouse execution with resource assignment
63V – Mobile RF Devices in WarehousingRF device support for warehouse operations
4A2 – Replenishment in WarehousingAutomatic replenishment control

None of these are required for basic bin-level putaway, picking, and stock tracking — but they extend the functional scope based on operational complexity.

entry.title: Re: How to hide the checkbox cell in Quote Table?
entry.content:
Hi @tdhirendra3221 ,

The checkboxes reappearing when you change the page size isn't a flaw in your condition — access levels set on quote table cells aren't persisted; they have to be reapplied every time the table is drawn. An action that redraws the able, like changing the rows-per-page, appears to reset any cell that isn't actively re-set back to its default (visible/editable) state, which is why the checkboxes come back.

The fix: keep the logic in Before Quote Rendering, but apply your hide condition to every row in the table, not just the visible page, and treat it as something that re-runs on every render rather than a one-time setup. If the checkbox still fights you, setting the cell read-only and unchecked when the adjacent cell is empty tends to hold up across re-renders better than hiding it.

entry.title: Re: How abap2UI5 Complements RAP and Fiori Elements – Now Also as a Custom Control
entry.content:
Hi @AlexandrePassarelli ,

thanks for the questions, they help to get the customer perspective and to see where we need to adjust or extend abap2UI5. Therefore I also added the information to the documentation (links at the end).

Answers in short:

  1. Every user who can reach the abap2UI5 ICF node can start every app, like starting a report in se38 without an authorization group. Therefore I recommend putting an authorization check right at the beginning of the main method of every app.
  2. abap2UI5 is on a stable level, so I don’t think a lot of updates are needed. Take the latest GitHub tag, and when you want to upgrade, e.g. in a year, just pull it into DEV, run your tests and then transport it to production, as you would with any other ABAP framework. If you run into problems, you can simply pull the previous tag again.
  3. abap2UI5 runs stateless, and it is fast, because nearly everything runs in the backend and the browser only renders. So far no performance issues are known, but please create an issue as soon as you find one.

Below are more detailed answers from Claude. Thanks again, and happy to take more questions here.

Best regards


--------

1. Authorization per app

The class name and the parameters come from the browser, so they are user input. Whoever reaches the service node can send any class name, just like with ?app_start= on the normal abap2UI5 page. The framework only checks that the class implements z2ui5_if_app, and drafts are bound to the user who created them. Who may run what is decided in plain ABAP:

  • The ICF node decides who reaches abap2UI5 at all: logon, SSO, S_ICF. For separate areas, create a node of your own (a handler class calling z2ui5_cl_ui5_http_handler=>run( server )) and point the control’s endpoint property at it.
  • The app class decides who may run it: an AUTHORITY-CHECK at the start of main( ). This is the recommended check, because it holds however the class is started: its own page, the launchpad, an object page section or nav_app_call( ).

An allowlist in the HTTP handler cannot work reliably: the class name only travels in the body of the first request, and later roundtrips carry none. The question also revealed a wrong example in the docs, which is fixed now.

Also important for embedded sections: the parameters are user input too. A credit check for order 4711 can be started with any other number, so the class should check the object as well (e.g. the sales organization). A CDS view with access control or EML on the RAP business object does that for you; a plain SELECT on the table does not.

2. Upgrades

No special regression process is needed. An abap2UI5 upgrade is an abapGit pull and a transport like any other custom code, so it gets the same QAS test as a SAPUI5 upgrade or a support package, which also change every Fiori app at once. Frontend and backend always come from the same system, so the embedding adds no new risk. If you want more control, pin a release, or keep the embedded sections on a second, renamed installation behind their own endpoint.

3. Sessions and performance

abap2UI5 is stateless by default: between two clicks there is no open ABAP session and no work process is held. Each container keeps one draft row in Z2UI5_T_01 (expires after 4 hours by default), so three containers are three rows, not three sessions. Opening the page costs one GET for the frontend plus one POST per container; after that a container only sends a request when the user acts in it.

So the speed of a section is mostly the speed of its own main( ): keep the start cheap and put expensive parts behind a button. There is no published benchmark for several containers, but since 1.147.0 the roundtrip monitor shows the time per class and the Admin Cockpit the p95 per app, which is the number to look at on QAS. One thing to avoid: set_session_stateful( ) in an embedded app, which would pin one work process per user and container.

Documentation:

  • Running it in production: https://abap2ui5.github.io/docs/advanced/fiori.html#running-it-in-production
  • Authorization: https://abap2ui5.github.io/docs/configuration/authorization.html

entry.title: Re: how to Handle a Assertion_failed Dump in SAP ABAP ?
entry.content:
A practical approach is to isolate each order in a separate RFC call so that a failure in one order does not stop the remaining processing.

DATA: lv_message TYPE string.

LOOP AT lt_orders INTO DATA(ls_order).

  CALL FUNCTION 'Z_PROCESS_SINGLE_ORDER'
    DESTINATION 'NONE'
    EXPORTING
      iv_order = ls_order-vbeln
    EXCEPTIONS
      system_failure        = 1 MESSAGE lv_message
      communication_failure = 2 MESSAGE lv_message
      OTHERS                = 3.

  IF sy-subrc <> 0.
    "Log the failed order and continue processing
    WRITE: / 'Order:', ls_order-vbeln,
             'Error:', lv_message.
    CONTINUE.
  ENDIF.

ENDLOOP.

Important: The function module must be RFC-enabled. This approach does not fix the underlying assertion failure. Check transaction ST22 to identify the root cause, and carefully handle transaction and rollback requirements.

Create Attachment in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition
1. Storage Location

The Attachment Service in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition is a reusable UI component that can be consumed by any SAP Fiori application to attach documents (e.g., PDFs, images, videos, plain text files) to business objects. [1] [2]

Regarding where attachments are physically stored, the storage location depends on which Generic Object Services (GOS) service is used to create the attachment: [3]

  • "Create Attachment" (SAPoffice/GOS attachment): By default, the physical document is stored in the SOFFCONT1 database table. A link entry is created in the SRGBTBREL table. However, it can also be redirected to an external content server if configured. [4] [3]
  • "Store Business Document" (ArchiveLink attachment): The physical document is stored on a content server configured in transaction OAC0, with the link maintained in TOA01/02/03/HR tables. [4] [3]

For SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition specifically, one community response indicates that attachments are stored on BTP (SAP Business Technology Platform), in a special section reserved for this purpose — without requiring any additional action or separate BTP service purchase. [5]

 

2. Pricing & Storage Threshold
  • Per-file size limit: Each individual file uploaded via the Attachment Service has a maximum size of 100 MB. Attempting to upload a file larger than this will result in an error. [7] [8]
    • As a workaround, a file exceeding 100 MB can be split into multiple parts (e.g., splitting a 200 MB PDF into two 100 MB PDFs) and attached separately. [7]
  • Total storage — no technical limit: There is no technical storage limit for total attachments in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. [9] [8]
  • Commercially included storage: The amount of storage commercially included depends on your contract type and subscription. The storage consumed by attachments counts against your subscription's storage allocation. [5] [9]
    • For specific details on your included storage allocation and any costs for extending beyond it, you should check your contract details with your SAP Sales contact or Account Executive. [9] [10]
    • If you need to extend storage beyond what is included in your default subscription, this can be discussed with your SAP account team to add an additional storage subscription. [5]

In summary: Creating attachments via the standard Attachment Service is included in the core SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition subscription — no separate BTP/DMS license purchase is required for basic attachment functionality. [5] However, storage consumed does count against your contracted storage allocation, and any storage beyond that allocation would need to be discussed with your SAP account team for additional subscription. [5] [9]

entry.title: Off-Neo migration of HTML5 Applications — Now with AI Skills
entry.content:
Migrating HTML5 Applications from Neo to Application Frontend Service — Now with AI Skills

SAP Neo is approaching end of life, and if you have HTML5 applications hosted there, you already know you need to move them to the multi-cloud environment. Application Frontend service is the natural destination — it brings back the simplicity and flexibility that Neo developers valued, now built on the multi-cloud foundation.

While SAP Business Application Studio provides a number of tools to assist with migration, the process is still mostly manual.  It can take a few hours for a simple application and up to days for a large-scale application.

We are happy to share a set of AI skills we built to automate most of this work.

Check out these earlier posts for more background about Application Frontend service:

  • Introducing Application Frontend Service
  • Simple UI Applications with Application Frontend Service
  • Moving HTML5 Applications to Application Frontend Service

What Are These AI Skills?

The skill focuses is migration from SAP Neo, but it can also migrate applications based on HTML5 Repository that use a managed approuter or standalone approuter. It targets Cloud Foundry or Kyma runtimes and supports both XSUAA and IAS authentication.

The package ships with three skills, each covering a different phase of the migration lifecycle:

/appfront:migrate analyses your existing HTML5 project, proposes a migration plan, waits for your approval, and then executes all the configuration changes. It never modifies your original project — it copies your original project to a new folder appfront-migrated/ and all changes are done to this copy.

/appfront:validate validates your migrated project configuration for correctness and deployment readiness. It goes through mta.yaml, xs-app.json, xs-security.json, and service bindings, and reports any issues against a known-good checklist. It can also connect to a live deployed application and validate it at runtime.

/appfront:cleanup is used if you want to completely roll back all changes done with the skill. It un-deploys any deployed applications and any related service instances and removes the local output folder. It always asks before any destructive step and never touches your original source project.

The skills are open source and available on GitHub: https://github.com/SAP-samples/html5-applications-migration-skills-for-sap-btp.

What Does the Skill Actually Do?

When you run /appfront:migrate on a Neo HTML5 project, the skill works through the migration in phases:

First, it reads and analyses your source files — neo-app.json, neo-mta.yaml, and manifest.json — and builds a complete picture of your routing, security constraints, and destinations. It then presents you with a migration plan: exactly which files will be created, which will be modified, and which Neo-specific artifacts will be removed. Nothing changes until you approve.

Once you confirm, the skill generates the full Application Frontend configuration:

  • xs-app.json — translated your neo-app.json routes and configurations
  • xs-security.json — Neo security constraints mapped to XSUAA scopes, role templates, and role collections
  • mta.yaml — with a content deployer module for deploying the application resources to Application Frontend

It also updates manifest.json, fixes the UI5 bootstrap path in index.html, and removes Grunt-based build artifacts that are no longer needed.

After generating the files, a built-in critic reviews the output against a checklist to identify common misconfigurations before you deploy.

Note: some steps still require manual action in the BTP cockpit — destination credentials with secrets are not exported from Neo for security reasons, so you will need to add those manually after import.

How Much Time Does It Save?

The table below provides an estimated comparison of the time needed to migrate applications manually and with the help of the AI skills, highlighting the potential time savings for applications of different sizes:

App size

Manual effort

Skill-assisted

Time saved

Small (1–3 routes, simple roles)

~3 hours

~30 min

~85%

Medium (4–10 routes, multiple roles)

~1 day (8 h)

~1.5 hours

~82%

Large (10+ routes, complex roles, WorkZone)

1–2 days

~4 hours

~75%

Note that end-to-end functional testing of your business logic is not included in these estimates. It requires developer or end user involvement and takes the same time regardless of how the technical migration was done.

 Mass Migration

The skills support mass migration of applications. If you have multiple applications with similar characteristics, you can run the skills to migrate all of them in one go. During the process, you can consolidate applications under the same business solution and MTA deployment or keep them completely independent. Simply answer the questions presented by the skill and, if needed, provide instructions in natural language to fine-tune the migration.

 Prerequisites and How to Get It

To use the migration skills, you will need:

  • AI Coding tool like Claude Code installed and connected to an LLM service
  • An SAP BTP subaccount with subscription to Application Frontend service
  • Cloud Foundry CLI  installed and logged in to your target org and space
  • MBT (Cloud MTA Build Tool) installed: npm install -g mbt
  • [Optional] Application Frontend CLI (afctl) installed and logged in for fetching the application URL after deployment: npm install -g @SAP/appfront-cli

Detailed prerequisite list and installation instructions are available in the README file. The skills were built with Claude Code in mind, but they can be installed and used in other coding tools like GitHub Copilot.

Once the skills are installed navigate to your project directory and run /appfront:migrate to get started.

To sum up

If you still have HTML5 applications running in the SAP Neo environment, now is the time to migrate them to SAP multi-cloud. The good news is that, with AI skills like the ones above, the process has become much easier.
Give it a try and let me know in the comments how it worked for you. If you have suggestions for improvement, the best approach would be to contribute them directly to the project’s Git repository.

entry.title: Dispute Resolution for Vendor Invoices: MCP Server App Designed in Hours, Not Developed in Months
entry.content:
From sales orders to supplier invoices

The second business AI app on our SAP ECC system works blocked supplier invoices, and it took one day to build.

In Part 1, Stop Building SAP Apps: Business AI Applications On Demand with an Ontology-Based MCP Server, we showed the Sales Representative Release Desk. Sales reps work blocked sales orders before the cancel date, and SAP suggests a decision for each order: release, extend, partial ship or cancel. The desk runs live on SAP ECC through Skybuffer AI, our ontology-based MCP server inside SAP.

This part takes the same approach to finance. The Invoice Dispute Desk resolves supplier invoices that SAP blocked for payment. This time the MCP server had no tools for invoice disputes yet, so the AI agent wrote them in ABAP, registered them in SAP and then built the app on top.

That is the advantage of the ontology approach: our MCP server describes SAP to the AI as business tools, not as OData services. When a use case needs more live SAP data or another action in SAP, the autonomous AI agent adds that tool to the server's registry. So apps like this are designed with the business unit in a workshop, in hours, not developed over weeks or months.

The problem: blocked invoices hold cash and burn discounts

Every blocked invoice is cash the treasury can't plan and, often, a cash discount that lapses while it waits.

Logistics invoice verification blocks a supplier invoice for payment when it doesn't match the purchase order and the goods receipt: a price above the order, more billed than received, goods that never arrived, or a manual hold. Duplicates add to the pile. Clearing each one means switching between MRBR, ME23N, MIGO, the vendor's email thread and a spreadsheet of who promised what.

On our demo system the board opened with seven blocked invoices worth 32,902.24 EUR. Of that, 6,976.00 EUR was in dispute, and 637.16 EUR of cash discount was at risk on six invoices that lose it within five days.

The app: one desk from diagnosis to release

The Invoice Dispute Desk puts every blocked invoice on one board, says what to do next, and lets the clerk do it with one tap and a confirmation.

The board

The board: tiles for cash, disputes and discounts, a stage rail and the worklist

Five tiles show what is at stake: invoices blocked for payment, the amount in dispute, the cash discount at risk, cases waiting on vendors, and invoices ready to release. A stage rail moves each invoice from New to Vendor contacted, Waiting, Ready to release and Done. Filters such as "Discount ≤ 5 days" put the money first.

Each row states the issue in plain words ("Wood Glue: 18.90 vs PO 18.00"), the days left for the cash discount, the case status and SAP's suggestion.

Diagnosis and a suggested next step

An invoice with SAP's suggestion and the three-way match per line

Opening an invoice shows the three-way match per line: ordered, received and billed quantity, PO price against billed price, and the amount over the order. A rules engine picks one next step and explains it with the amounts: release, request a credit memo, accept the price, post the goods receipt, reverse a duplicate or investigate.

For Halvorsen's wood glue it found a newer purchase order at the billed price, so it suggests accepting the price rather than fighting it.

Proof one tap away

Drill-down from the invoice into the purchase order and the prices on other orders

Every purchase order, goods receipt, invoice, vendor and material number is a link that opens live SAP data inside the drawer. Tapping the order shows three newer Halvorsen orders at 18.90 EUR, so the price change is visible before anyone accepts it.

Act, with a confirmation

Each action opens a short form and posts nothing until the clerk reviews and confirms:

  • release the payment block, as MRBR does
  • reverse the invoice, as MR8M does
  • accept the billed price: the PO price changes, then the invoice is released
  • post the vendor's credit memo or the goods receipt

A drafted vendor email, sent from SAP and recorded on the case

For a real dispute, the desk drafts the vendor email from a template per dispute type. It sends the email from SAP and moves the case to Vendor contacted, with a follow-up in three days.

Every step on record

The dispute case with owner and follow-up date, and its audit trail

Each disputed invoice gets a case in SAP with a reason, an owner, a follow-up date and an append-only audit trail of who did what. Resolved invoices move to Done, so the team sees what is left and what was settled.

How it was built in one day

Nobody opened a development project. The desk came out of one conversation between me and an AI assistant (Claude), connected to our SAP ECC system through Skybuffer AI.

One MCP server inside SAP builds the tools and runs the app

The assistant builds through the development tools, and the desk runs on the business tools they produce, both through the same server inside SAP.

Skybuffer AI also follows the SAP-endorsed architecture for AI agents: the same MCP server can be consumed through the MCP Gateway in SAP Integration Suite on SAP BTP. That brings SAP's governance layer for AI agents on top, with authentication, rate limiting and observability.

The brief fit in a few lines: build a dispute resolution desk for vendor invoices in SAP ERD. Be creative: create ABAP classes and register them as tools where needed, refresh the MCP server, and create or clean the master and transaction data the demo needs.

From there Claude took over as my autonomous AI development agent, empowered by Skybuffer AI tools. ABAP Code Intelligence, one of those tools, guarded code integrity, so the new ABAP fits our existing code. The agent worked through SAP the way a developer would, only faster:

  1. Explore. It read the framework conventions and the existing tools in the MCP server, then the invoice landscape: RBKP, RSEG, EKBE and the blocked-invoice table RBKP_BLOCKED.
  2. Design. It proposed the toolset and the data model: a dispute case table, an audit trail table and a rules engine for the three-way match.
  3. Build. It created the tables and the ABAP classes through the MCP server's development tools, activated them and recorded them in a workbench transport.
  4. Register. It registered each class as an MCP tool, in a customizing transport, and refreshed the MCP server.
  5. Test live. It created four demo vendors with .example mailboxes, purchase orders, goods receipts and invoices, and tested every tool against them in SAP.
  6. Build the app. It built the desk on top of the tools and tested it end to end.

I reviewed the plan and the results. Every generated ABAP file header says so: requirements and review by me, design and implementation by Claude.

What the AI generated in SAP

The assistant generated nine MCP tools in ABAP, a rules engine and two tables.

X-ray of the desk: which generated tool sits behind each part of the screen

MCP tool What it does Writes to SAP

get_disputed_vendor_invoicesThe worklist: blocked invoices, open cases, totals and discount at riskno
get_vendor_invoice_dispute_detailOne invoice: three-way match per line, suggestion, case and audit trailno
manage_vendor_invoice_disputeOpens, updates, annotates and closes a dispute casecase tables only
post_vendor_invoicePosts an invoice or the vendor's credit memo, linked to the disputed invoicean invoice document, as MIRO
accept_invoice_priceChanges the PO price to the billed price, through BAPI_PO_CHANGEPO net price
release_blocked_vendor_invoiceRemoves the payment block, optionally moving the baseline date to keep the discountpayment block
reverse_vendor_invoiceReverses a duplicate or wrong invoice, through BAPI_INCOMINGINVOICE_CANCELa reversal document
get_purchase_order_historyA PO with its history, its invoices and the prices of the same material on other ordersno
get_material_documentA goods receipt with quantities, values and reversalsno

Behind the tools sit the rules engine class /SKYBFR/CL_YAI_VIDSP, the case table /SKYBFR/YAIVIDC and the audit trail table /SKYBFR/YAIVIDL. The engine holds the three-way match, the rules and the open posting period. Both tables are also published as data sources, so the assistant can answer questions such as "which vendors take longest to reply?"

The desk also reuses tools the server already had: send_email, post_goods_receipt, get_vendor_details and get_material_stock. Everything sits in a workbench transport and a customizing transport, which go through normal change management.

Same pattern, second process

Both desks follow one pattern: a worklist of what SAP blocked, a diagnosis with a suggested decision, one-tap actions behind a confirmation, and a record of who did what. Only the business content changes.

  Sales Representative Release Desk (Part 1) Invoice Dispute Desk (Part 2)

ProcessSales orders on a delivery blockSupplier invoices blocked for payment
Who works itSales repsAccounts payable clerks
Deadline on screenThe order's cancel dateThe cash discount date
SAP suggestsRelease, extend, partial ship or cancel, from the ATP check and inbound receiptsRelease, credit memo, accept price, goods receipt, reverse or investigate, from the three-way match
Stages8 steps, from identify to follow upNew, vendor contacted, waiting, ready to release, done
Changes in SAPSales order changes through change_sales_orderRelease, reversal, PO price, credit memo, goods receipt, case log
Contact notes keptIn the page's shared storeIn SAP tables, with an audit trail
Partner emailDrafted for the rep to sendSent from SAP
MCP tools used713: 9 generated, 4 reused

The difference that matters: the Sales Representative Release Desk ran on tools the MCP server already had. The Invoice Dispute Desk needed new ones, and the AI built them in the same day.

Security and governance

The desk changes SAP only through tools that check the user's SAP authorizations, and only after the user confirms.

  • SAP authorizations apply. Each tool checks the authorizations of the person using it: M_RECH_BUK for invoice verification, M_BEST_EKO and M_BEST_EKG for purchase orders, M_MSEG_WMB for goods movements. With a direct connection, people sign in to the MCP server with their own SAP user through single sign-on.
  • Nothing posts without a confirmation. Every write opens a form and waits for Review and confirm. Postings go through standard SAP logic, such as BAPI_PO_CHANGE and BAPI_INCOMINGINVOICE_CANCEL.
  • The page calls only what it declares. The desk lists the SAP tools it may use, and Claude asks each user before the first call.
  • No copy of SAP data. The desk reads live from SAP each time it opens. Cases and the audit trail are SAP tables.
  • Normal change management. Generated objects travel in transports, so they are reviewed and moved through the landscape like any other development.
  • Any model. Skybuffer AI works with Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or a self-hosted model. We built this desk with Claude.

What's next

Two processes, two desks, one MCP server: the next business app is a conversation away, and it can bring its own ABAP tools with it.

The 3-minute video shows the Invoice Dispute Desk on a phone, from the blocked board to the x-ray of the generated tools.

Which process should we take on next? Tell us in the comments. Questions about the ABAP side, the rules engine or the MCP server are welcome there too.

entry.title: Re: Unable to Set Maintenance Order to Commercially Compl...
entry.content:
The KO020 check evaluates whether any vendor open items with a down payment special G/L indicator remain open against the order. This can occur even when the down payment appears settled at the business document level, if the underlying Financial Accounting (FI) special G/L item was not correctly cleared during invoice processing. In scenarios involving Advanced Down Payment Processing with an externally procured service PO, this typically happens when the down payment request was not linked to the Purchasing Document and Purchasing Doc. Item at the time of creation — preventing the system from offering or applying the correct down payment clearing during invoice verification.

Please ask your Finance or AP team to carry out the following verification and correction steps:

  1. Check for open FI items: Open the Manage Supplier Line Items app. In the selection criteria, include Special G/L transactions (indicator A for down payments and F for down payment requests) and filter by Open Items for the relevant vendor. Verify whether any line items related to the PO assigned to Maintenance Order still appear as open.
  2. Verify the clearing status in the PO down payment monitor: Open the Monitor Purchase Order Down Payments app (F2877) and search for the relevant Purchase Order. Confirm that the Down Payment, Down Payment Request, and Invoice columns all reflect full coverage with a green/cleared status indicator. A non-cleared or partial status here confirms the issue.
  3. Reset the clearing if needed: If step 1 reveals an open FI special G/L item, open the Reset Cleared Items app (F2223). Locate the clearing document that cleared the down payment request, select it, and choose Reset and Reverse. This re-opens the down payment request as an open item in FI.
  4. Verify the Purchasing Document reference on the request: Open the Manage Supplier Down Payment Requests app (F1688) and confirm that the down payment request contains both the Purchasing Document number and the Purchasing Doc. Item. If these fields are blank, please update them with the correct PO number and item reference.
  5. Re-process the supplier invoice: Using the Create Supplier Invoice – Advanced app (MIRO) with reference to the same PO, you should now see the Down Payment Clearing button available. Use it to explicitly clear the down payment against the invoice before saving.

For further reference: KBA 2130927 (KO020 error even when no open down payments appear visible), KBA 3547892 (Down Payment Clearing button missing when PO reference is absent), KBA 3412907 (PO down payment amount not updated when PO reference not maintained).

Hope this helps.

Nick

entry.title: SAP Digital Manufacturing: Can DM-only dispensing order stock be consumed by an ERP process order?
entry.content:
Hello SAP Community,

We are evaluating a pre-weighing and dispensing scenario in SAP Digital Manufacturing integrated with SAP S/4HANA. We would appreciate guidance on whether the following design is supported.

Business requirement

Raw materials are weighed and divided into containers in a separate dispensing area, then stored and later delivered to production.

  • The material code and batch must remain unchanged after dispensing.
  • Each container must have its own identifier and quantity for traceability.
  • Dispensing must not trigger ERP goods issue or goods receipt.
  • ERP consumption should occur only when the container is actually used in the manufacturing process order.

Proposed design — not yet validated

  1. Stage raw-material stock from S/4HANA to DM through movement type 311.
  2. Use a separate production order in DM to execute dispensing. The order header material is the same raw material being dispensed, and each SFC represents one container.
  3. Assemble the original raw-material inventory into the container SFC, reducing the original DM inventory without posting ERP consumption.
  4. Complete the SFC to generate container floor stock through internal DM goods receipt, retaining the original material and batch. Prevent ERP postings from this dispensing order.
  5. Later, consume the container Inventory ID in an ERP-origin process order using the Material Consumption plugin, triggering movement type 261 in S/4HANA.

For example, starting with 100 kg:

StageDM inventoryS/4HANA inventory
Before dispensingOriginal stock: 100 kg100 kg
After dispensing 10 kgOriginal stock: 90 kg; container stock: 10 kg100 kg
After consuming the container in the process orderOriginal stock: 90 kg; container stock: 0 kg90 kg, with one 261 posting

Documentation reviewed

  • Floor Stock Receipt: describes floor-stock generation upon SFC completion.
  • Floor Stock Consumption: describes consumption of transferred, received or generated floor stocks by ERP orders, including process orders.
  • Inventory Management Mode: describes stock creation following production-order SFC completion.
  • KBA 3778100: explains that DisableGR=true prevents ERP GR replication but does not suppress internal DM goods receipt. We understand that this setting alone does not prevent ERP goods issue.

These references describe the individual capabilities, but we have not confirmed the combined scenario above.

Questions

  1. Is this a supported design, particularly when the dispensing production order has no corresponding order in S/4HANA?
  2. Can its generated container stock be selected and consumed by an ERP-origin process order, with the correct 261 posting?
  3. What determines the generated stock’s origin, batch and storage location? Can the original raw-material batch be retained?
  4. How should integration be configured to prevent ERP GI/GR for dispensing while retaining normal ERP consumption for the process order?
  5. Are there restrictions related to inventory management mode or using the same material as both input and output? If this approach is unsuitable, what standard alternative would you recommend?

Any relevant SAP Notes, documentation or implementation experience would be appreciated.

Thank you.
