entry.title: Batch transfers in SAP B1 without selecting every batch
entry.content:
Environment: SAP Business One 10, Service Layer, SQL Server / HANA

Introduction

Moving batch-managed stock between warehouses in SAP Business One means selecting batches by hand for every line, which gets slow when items have many batches. This post shows how to prepare the whole transfer in one Excel sheet and post it through the Service Layer as a single document.

The problem

While working on an SAP project, I noticed how slow it is to move batch-managed stock between warehouses. Many items have several batches. In the Inventory Transfer window you have to open the batch selection and pick the batches for each line, one by one. DTW doesn’t make it easier, because the batch lines go in a separate file. Either way it takes hours, so I looked for a faster way.

The approach

The idea is to keep everything in one Excel sheet, with one row per item and batch. The columns the transfer needs are the item code, the batch number, the quantity to move, the source warehouse and the destination warehouse.

  1. Export the batches that have available stock. The export has the item code, batch number, quantities and the warehouse they are in. On SQL Server this is a read-only query. On HANA, I run a saved query inside B1 and export the result.
  2. Add two columns: Transfer Qty and To Whs.
  3. Fill them in only for the rows you want to move.
Item No.Batch NumberFrom WhsTo WhsTransfer Qty
ITEM2001BT101W8121
ITEM2001BT201W8122
ITEM2001BT301W812 3

The sheet can hold as many items as you need, and they all go into one document. Rows are grouped by item code, from-warehouse and to-warehouse. Each group becomes one line of the transfer, with its batches inside. Rows where both warehouses are the same are skipped. The three rows above become this one line:

 

{
  "DocDate": "2026-10-25",
  "StockTransferLines": [{
    "ItemCode": "ITEM2001", "Quantity": 6,
    "FromWarehouseCode": "01", "WarehouseCode": "W812",
    "BatchNumbers": [
      {"BatchNumber": "BT1", "Quantity": 1},
      {"BatchNumber": "BT2", "Quantity": 2},
      {"BatchNumber": "BT3", "Quantity": 3}
    ]
  }]
}

The batch quantities have to add up to the line quantity, and if the item belongs to a UoM group the line also needs a UoMEntry.

 

Posting and validation

After logging in through /b1s/v1/Login, the document is sent as a JSON POST to /b1s/v1/StockTransfers, or to /b1s/v1/StockTransferDrafts when it should be checked in SAP first. SAP validates it like any other entry and nothing touches the database directly. If SAP rejects the document, the error comes back as it is, so the row can be fixed and the run repeated.

Instead of a script, I built a small Windows app for this, called Batch Transfer. It runs separately from SAP and talks to it only through the Service Layer.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

A draft run on demo data: ITEM2001 moving from warehouse 01 to W812 with three batches.

Conclusion

Selecting batches line by line is slow when an item has many of them. With one Excel sheet, the whole transfer goes to SAP as a single Stock Transfer, validated like any other document. If a row is rejected, the error points to it, so you fix that row and run again.

Prepared by

Amirhossein Tonekaboni
SAP Business One Consultant

entry.title: Transition to SuccessFactors from non SAP system in an M&A engagement
entry.content:
Transition to SuccessFactors from non SAP system in an M&A engagement

Lift and shift or harmonize? A high-level guide to the critical focus areas

 

Applies when the parent runs on SAP SuccessFactors and acquired company runs on a different HR platform like Workday.

Summary

When an acquired company runs on a non-SAP HCM platform and the parent runs on SAP SuccessFactors, the integration is rarely a single decision. It is a series of area-by-area choices between two paths: lift and shift the acquired company's way of working or harmonize onto the parent's standards.

Two ways to bring an acquired population into the parent system

LIFT AND SHIFT

HARMONIZE

•     Keep the acquired structures

•     Fastest path and lowest Day 1 risk (based upon TSA timeline)

•     Honors commitments to employees

•     Creates clean-up work after go-live

•     Adopt the parent's standards

•     Unified structure, cleaner analytics

•     Needs HR and business alignment

•     Higher change impact for employees on day 1

 

Part A: Foundation Areas

These areas define how people, jobs, and organizations are represented in SuccessFactors Employee Central.

1. Job Architecture

Job codes, job families, levels and grades, job profiles, titles

Lift and shift

Carry the acquired company's job codes and titles into SuccessFactors as-is, utilizing existing job families and adding new.

Harmonize

Map all acquired roles into the parent's existing job architecture before load.

Focus areas

•     Mapping Workday job profiles to EC job classifications

•     Preserving FLSA/exempt status and EEO and other compliance fields

•     Level calibration, pay range impact, and title changes if harmonizing

•     Impact on compa-ratio for compensation module

Best practice

Lift and shift for Day 1 so harmonization can happen later without rework, unless the role mapping is obvious and already approved.

 

2. Organization Structure and Legal Entities

Supervisory orgs vs. departments, cost centers, legal entities, positions

Lift and shift

Recreate the acquired structure as a standalone branch in the parent's org tree.

Harmonize

Fold teams into the parent's departments, cost centers, and reporting lines.

Focus areas

•     Legal entity and cost center setup (finance and payroll dependencies)

•     Position management vs. non-position models

•     Manager hierarchy accuracy and approval chains (OrgLab can be used to define future state reporting structure)

•     Employees with dotted-line or matrix relationships

Best practice

Keep a clear structure as much as possible at go-live, then you can align in planned waves based upon finance and legal entity decisions.

 

3. Compensation and Benefits Structures

Pay grades, salary ranges, bonus plans, benefit plans, merit cycles

Lift and shift

Preserve existing pay structures and plan eligibility to honor commitments.

Harmonize

Move employees to the parent's structures and programs.

Focus areas

•     There may be Legal or contractual obligations to maintain pay and benefits for a defined period

•     Country-specific compensation plans

•     Integration with payroll and benefits vendors

•     Alignment of merit and bonus cycles with the go-live

Best practice

Cover the existing terms at transition. Harmonization can be done later with job architecture harmonization

 

4. Business Rules and Workflows

Approvals, hire/term/transfer rules,event reasons

Lift and shift

Replicate acquired company processes in SuccessFactors as closely as possible.

Harmonize

Adopt the parent's standard workflows and rules.

Focus areas

•     Workday business processes do not map one-to-one to SF workflows and business rules

•     Defaults such as work schedule hours at hire

•     Termination logic and workflow conditions

•     Event and reason code alignment

Best practice

Default to the parent's standard processes. Replicating acquired company logic in SF usually adds complexity at go-live. Make exceptions only for legal or country needs for a successful go-live

 

5. Security and Access (RBP)

Role-based permissions, groups, sensitive data, single sign-on

Lift and shift

Replicate the acquired company's security roles.

Harmonize

Build access on the parent's role and group model.

Focus areas

•     Rebuild in RBP groups and roles rather than copying Workday/third party security to avoid continuing security policies that were not effective

•     Target population groups for the acquired company

•     Country-based restrictions

•     Tighter controls sensitive data such as dependents, national IDs

Best practice

Always harmonize. Replicating another platform's security model is not recommended

 

6. Country Configuration and Compliance

New countries, statutory fields, data privacy, regulatory reporting

Lift and shift

Configure acquired countries as stand-alone setups with their own picklists, fields, and templates.

Harmonize

Align to the parent's country configurations where they already exist.

Focus areas

•     Statutory fields and local labor law requirements

•     New country setup where the parent has no footprint

•     Document and contract templates by country

•     Regulatory reporting continuity (for example EEO and VETS-4212 in the US)

•     Data privacy requirements such as GDPR

Best practice

Build a country-by-country readiness checklist with local HR and Legal sign-off. Reuse the parent's configuration where it exists and add only the gaps.

 

7. Historical Data

Effective-dated history, archives, retention, right of access

Lift and shift

Load as much history as the data model allows.

Harmonize

Load current state record into SuccessFactors

Focus areas

•     Full history should not be converted

•     Retention policy and who can access the archive after transition

•     GDPR right of access

•     Former employees' future needs: tax, immigration, benefits, legal matters

Best practice

This is often underestimated and surfaces late, usually when a former employee or auditor asks for records that no longer exist in the new system. Define the retention and access model early: where history lives, who can access it, and how former employees can request their records.

 

Part B: Talent Modules

8. Performance and Goals Management (PMGM)

Goals, review cycles, ratings, calibration, feedback, development plans

Performance touches pay, promotion, and how employees feel about being evaluated by a new company. It is also closely scrutinized by works councils.

 

Lift and shift

Build separate templates, rating scales, and cycle dates in SF for the acquired population.

Harmonize

Assign acquired employees to the parent's existing forms, scale, and calendar.

Focus areas

•     Template and permission assignment by population

•     Rating scale crosswalk (for example 5-point to 4-point or 5-point to 5-point) – determine how past ratings map

•     Route maps and calibration sessions that include the new group

•     RBP visibility for ratings and feedback

•     Performance history of employees

•     Complete in flight cycle in legacy system

Best Practice

Honor the in-flight cycle through completion, then onboard the acquired population into the parent's process at the start of the next cycle. Build a rating scale crosswalk and archive historical ratings with controlled access. In Scenario B, skip building a temporary SF process if the parent will not use that module.

 

 

9. Recruitment and Talent Acquisition

Requisitions, candidates, offers, onboarding handoff, compliance reporting

Hiring does not pause on go-live day. Open requisitions, in-flight candidates, and offers must continue, and offers are legally sensitive.

 

Lift and shift

Create separate requisition templates, approval flows, and offer letter templates for the acquired population.

Harmonize

Use the parent's templates, workflows, and career site.

Focus areas

•     Requisition and offer approval workflows

•     Requisition templates tied to job architecture

•     Onboarding handoff to EC and country-specific fields

Best Practice

Harmonize while protecting in-flight offers.

10. Learning

Catalog, curricula, assignments, transcripts, compliance training

Lift and shift

Migrate the acquired company's courses, curricula, and assignments.

Harmonize

Move the acquired population into the parent's catalog and assignment model.

Focus areas

•     Completion records and certifications that are compliance-critical

•     Assignment profiles and exclusion rules, so parent-company mandatory assignments do not flood the acquired population unintentionally

•     Content licensing

•     Access for employees and managers

Best practice

Migrate completion records for compliance-critical items only. Use exclusion rules to control assignments, then phase the acquired population into the parent catalog on a planned schedule.

 

Part C: Operations and Experience

These areas keep people paid, informed, and productive from the first day on the new platform.

11. Time Off and Work Schedules

Leave policies, accruals, balances, holiday calendars, default hours

Lift and shift

Recreate the acquired policies and accrual rules, and carry over balances.

Harmonize

Move to the parent's policies.

Focus areas

•     Policy gaps in countries where the parent has no equivalent (manual tracking or a vendor solution)

•     Work schedule defaults, such as hours defaulting at new hire

•     Configure work schedules for time off calculations

•     Holiday calendars by location

Best practice

Lift and shift at go-live. Changing leave policies mid-transition can create issues. Flag country gaps early and decide on manual or vendor tracking.

 

12. Employee Experience and Language Support

Self-service, mobile, documents, language, help desk, communications

Lift and shift

Provide a separate portal or landing experience for the acquired population.

Harmonize

Move employees to the parent's portal, mobile app, and support model.

Focus areas

•     Employee and manager self-service readiness

•     Language support gaps in the UI and translated job aids

•     Help desk and case routing for the new population

•     Communications and training before and after cutover

Best practice

Use the parent's company experience, and close language gaps before go-live. Translated materials also support the works council conversation.

entry.content:
A nice retrospective, and 30 years is a genuine milestone. The thread from the first computer-based exams in 1996, through Learning Hub in 2014 and Credly badges, to the Stay Current program captures how certification shifted from a one-time pass to an ongoing credential.

The most interesting chapter is clearly the one that started in 2025: scenario-based, open-book assessments where candidates can use SAP Help, SAP Learning and Joule during the exam, with over 100 certifications already moved to the practical format. That is a bigger change than any previous milestone, because it tests how someone works rather than what they memorised. Would be good to see a follow-up with early data on pass rates and how employers are responding to the new format.

entry.title: SAP FI Posting Really Works From FB50 to BKPF, BSEG, and ACDOCA
entry.content:
For many SAP Finance consultants, posting a journal entry is one of the first activities we learn. Open FB50, enter the accounts and amounts, make sure debit equals credit, and post.

The result looks simple: debit one account and credit another. But what actually happens inside SAP when we click Post? Where does the document go? What is stored in BKPF? What is stored in BSEG? Why do we also have ACDOCA in SAP S/4HANA? And when troubleshooting a posting, which object should a functional consultant investigate?

In this walkthrough, we will follow one simple G/L posting from FB50 to the posted accounting document and then into the underlying accounting data. The objective is not just to post a journal entry, but to understand how the user-facing transaction relates to SAP's accounting structures.

Assume we need to record an office expense of USD 1,000. The simplified accounting entry is:

Line

Account

Debit

Credit

1

Reserve Defer'd Tax

$1,00

 

2

Payroll Bonus

 

$1,00

For this exercise, we use transaction FB50 - Enter G/L Account Document. The exact company code, G/L accounts, cost center, and other organizational values will depend on your sandbox.

Figure 1: Sample G/L journal entry entered using FB50

Figure 1 establishes the transaction used throughout this article. The header represents information that applies to the overall accounting document, while the lower section contains the accounting line items.

FB50 provides a single-screen way to enter a G/L account document. From the user's perspective, the transaction combines document-level information with line-item information.

Header information

  1. Company Code
  2. Document Date
  3. Posting Date
  4. Document Type
  5. Currency
  6. Reference
  7. Header Text

Line-item information

  1. G/L Account
  2. Debit or Credit Amount
  3. Tax Code
  4. Cost Center
  5. Profit Center
  6. Assignment
  7. Item Text

Other account assignments depending on configuration

This distinction becomes important later because the accounting document is not represented by one single table containing every field in exactly the same way.

Before Posting: SAP Validates the Document

Clicking Post does not mean SAP simply writes the screen values directly to the database. The document must first satisfy the posting controls and checks that apply to the transaction and configuration.

At a high level, think of the process as:

User Input → Validation → Derivation → Accounting Document Creation → Database Update

Depending on the scenario, SAP may evaluate items such as:

  1. Is the company code valid?
  2. Is the posting period open?
  3. Is the G/L account valid and open for posting?
  4. Are mandatory fields populated according to field status?
  5. Are account assignments such as cost center valid on the posting date?
  6. Do debits and credits balance?
  7. Are document-type and posting-key rules satisfied?
  8. Do validations, substitutions, or enhancements apply?

In our simple example, the document must balance: debit USD 1,000 and credit USD 1,000, producing a zero document balance.

Simulate Before Posting

Before posting, use the simulation functionality where appropriate. Simulation is useful because it allows you to review the accounting result before the document is committed.

Do not assume that the number of lines entered by the user will always equal the final accounting representation. More complex scenarios can introduce taxes, automatically generated lines, account determination, document splitting, or other ledger-relevant information.

 As shown in Figure 2, the simulation gives us a checkpoint: this is the accounting result we expect SAP to create when we post.

Post the Document

Once the document passes the relevant checks, click Post. SAP generates an accounting document number according to the configured number range.

Record the Company Code, Accounting Document Number, and Fiscal Year. These values become the key for the rest of the investigation.

 

 

Display the Posted Document in FB03

Before going to the database tables, first review the document from the functional user's perspective. Open FB03 and display the document that was just posted.

Figure 4 represents the posted document as a functional consultant would normally review it. We will now use the same document key to inspect the underlying accounting data.

 

First Stop: BKPF - Accounting Document Header

Open SE16N and enter table BKPF. Filter using the same Company Code, Accounting Document, and Fiscal Year.

Recommended selection:

BUKRS = <your company code>
BELNR = <your posted document number>
GJAHR = <fiscal year>

BKPF represents accounting document header information. Conceptually, it answers questions about the document as a whole.

Field

Meaning

BUKRS

Company Code

BELNR

Accounting Document Number

GJAHR

Fiscal Year

BUDAT

MONAT

USNAM

XBLNR

BKTXT

Document Header Text

From Figure 5, we can quickly identify the document type, dates, fiscal period, currency, originating transaction, and user-related header information. For many support investigations, BKPF is an efficient first checkpoint.

Second Stop: BSEG - Operational Accounting Items

Next, open SE16N for BSEG and use the same document key. Instead of one header record, you will see the operational accounting document items.

Field

Purpose

BUKRS

Company Code

BELNR

Accounting Document

GJAHR

Fiscal Year

BUZEI

Cost Center where applicable

PRCTR

Profit Center where applicable

The operational accounting items shown in Figure 6 should be compared with the lines previously displayed in FB03. This is the bridge between the user-facing accounting document and the technical representation of its entry items.

Enter ACDOCA - The Universal Journal

In SAP S/4HANA, the investigation should not stop at BSEG. Open SE16N for ACDOCA and filter the same accounting document.

ACDOCA is the Universal Journal line-item table. It brings together a broad set of accounting and reporting dimensions that are central to S/4HANA Finance.

Depending on your scenario and configuration, useful fields can include:

  1. RLDNR - Ledger
  2. RBUKRS - Company Code
  3. GJAHR - Fiscal Year
  4. BELNR - Accounting Document
  5. DOCLN - Universal Journal line item
  6. RACCT - G/L Account
  7. RCNTR - Cost Center
  8. PRCTR - Profit Center
  9. SEGMENT - Segment
  10. Relevant currency and amount fields for your posting

Is BSEG Replaced by ACDOCA?

A common simplification is: "In S/4HANA, ACDOCA replaced BSEG." That statement is too broad.

BSEG still exists and remains important for operational accounting-document information. ACDOCA represents the Universal Journal. A more useful troubleshooting model is:

BKPF → Document header
BSEG → Operational / entry-view accounting information
ACDOCA → Universal Journal and ledger-oriented accounting information

The correct object depends on the question you are trying to answer. Functional troubleshooting becomes faster when you first decide whether you are investigating the document header, operational line-item behavior, or the Universal Journal representation.

Entry View vs. General Ledger View

For a basic two-line posting, the entry view and the General Ledger representation may look very similar. However, more complex scenarios can introduce additional ledger-relevant information or generated lines.

Document splitting is a good example. A transaction entered with only a few business lines can result in additional lines in the General Ledger view so that required reporting dimensions remain balanced.

Compare BKPF, BSEG, and ACDOCA

Question

Start With

Who posted the document?

BKPF

What is the document type?

BKPF

What is the posting date?

BKPF

What transaction created it?

BKPF

What are the operational accounting items?

BSEG

What posting key / account type was used?

BSEG

What clearing or payment attributes are relevant?

BSEG

What is posted to a particular ledger?

ACDOCA

What cost center / profit center / segment is represented in the Universal Journal?

ACDOCA

Which Universal Journal dimensions were generated?

ACDOCA

The important lesson is not to troubleshoot an S/4HANA accounting document by looking at only one table. Start with the business question, and then select the object that represents that layer of the transaction.

Simplified Conceptual Flow

The following diagram should be created as a simple PowerPoint or diagram image and inserted into the blog. Label it as a simplified conceptual view so readers do not interpret it as the exact ABAP execution or physical database-write sequence.

Why This Matters During Production Support

Consider a support ticket: "The profit center is incorrect on accounting document 1900000123."

A stronger troubleshooting path is:

  1. Identify the document and header context in BKPF.
  2. Understand the operational accounting items in BSEG.
  3. Examine the Universal Journal representation in ACDOCA.
  4. Determine where the expected and actual values first diverge.

Functional Consultants Should Understand the Technical Layer

A functional consultant does not need to become an ABAP developer to benefit from understanding SAP's technical architecture. Knowing how to move from transaction to accounting document to database structures can dramatically improve troubleshooting.

Instead of asking only, "Why did SAP not populate the profit center?" a more precise investigation is: "Was the profit center present in the operational entry view, and what value ultimately reached the Universal Journal?"

Trace the responsible derivation, configuration, substitution, enhancement, or integration logic.

This approach can help with issues involving cost centers, profit centers, segments, currencies, clearing, document splitting, account determination, interfaces, substitutions, and enhancements.

Key Takeaways

  1. FB50 is only the starting point; SAP performs validation and derivation before a document is persisted.
  2. BKPF is the primary place to understand accounting document header information.
  3. BSEG remains relevant for operational accounting-document line items in S/4HANA.
  4. ACDOCA contains the Universal Journal line-item representation and ledger/reporting dimensions.
  5. The same accounting document should be traced across FB03, BKPF, BSEG, and ACDOCA to understand the complete picture.
  6. For support issues, identify the layer where the value first differs before jumping directly to configuration or code.

entry.title: M&A Engagements: Works Council Engagement - A Gating Item for HR System Migrations
entry.content:
HR TECHNOLOGY M&A INTEGRATION

Works Council Engagement: A Gating Item for HR

System Migrations

Co-determination, consultation, and approval rights over HR systems and employee data

 

Who this is for: program leads, HRIS teams, Legal, and Privacy teams moving an acquired workforce onto a new HR platform (for example from Workday into SAP SuccessFactors) where acquired employees sit in countries with works councils.

1. Why this is a gating item

Works council engagement is not a lift and shift vs. harmonize choice. In countries with works councils, the council often has legal rights to be informed, consulted, or to approve a new HR system before employee data can move. Missing this can delay go-live regardless of how ready the technology is.

The core message

A system can be fully configured, tested, and signed off by the business, and still be blocked at the last step. Treat works council approval as a formal go-live readiness criterion, owned and tracked like any other critical-path item.

 

What is at stake if it is skipped

Country example

Possible consequence of proceeding without the required process

Germany

The council can seek injunctive relief to stop use of a monitoring-capable system until co-determination is respected, and the matter can end up before a conciliation committee.

Netherlands

A decision taken without required consent can be declared void if the council invokes this in time, and the council can contest the decision.

France

Courts have ordered deployments of new tools suspended until the information and consultation procedure is completed, in some cases with daily penalties.

All countries

Delayed go-live, loss of trust with the workforce, rework of design decisions, and reputational and legal exposure.

 

2. Understand the rights you are dealing with

Not every council right is the same. The strength of the right changes what you must prepare and how long the process can take. In practice, three levels matter.

The spectrum of works council rights

INFORM

→

CONSULT

→

CONSENT

Council receives the facts

before decisions are final

 

Council gives an opinion

and the employer must hear it

before deciding

 

No lawful rollout without

agreement, or a substitute

ruling or conciliation

Typical for: early information on planned technical systems (for example Germany, Sec. 90 BetrVG)

 

Typical for: France, where the CSE is informed and consulted on new technology and on tools that monitor activity

 

Typical for: Germany (Sec. 87 BetrVG) and the Netherlands (Art. 27 WOR) for systems that can monitor or that process personnel data

Rights differ by country and by what the system does. Always confirm with local counsel.

 

Why HR systems usually trigger these rights

  • An HR platform holds personnel data, and rules about processing and protecting that data are often subject to council rights.
  • Several statutes look at capability, not intent. A system that can observe or record behavior or performance can trigger consent rights even if the employer promises not to use it that way.
  • Talent modules go further. Performance, goals, and assessment criteria are frequently treated as evaluation schemes, which have their own consent or consultation rules.
  • Analytics, dashboards, and AI-assisted features can widen the scope. Switching a feature on later can reopen the discussion.

 

How the level shapes your plan

Level

What it means for the program

Plan for

Inform

No veto, but early notice builds trust and avoids disputes later

•     Brief the council early

•     Share a dossier summary and a named contact

Consult

The council's opinion must be heard before the decision is taken, so timing matters

•     Allow a real review period

•     Document how feedback was handled

•     Decide only after consultation closes

Consent

The council can withhold agreement, which may lead to negotiation, conciliation, or a court route

•     Treat as critical path

•     Negotiate a written agreement

•     Prepare a contingency per country

 

3. What works councils typically focus on

Councils generally ask the same core questions, even when the legal basis differs. Preparing a clear answer to each, in writing and in the local language, is the single most effective way to shorten the process.

Topic

What the council asks

What to bring

Data

What employee data is collected, what moves to the new system, and why it is needed

•     Field-level data inventory: field, source, target, purpose

•     Rationale for each category, and what is not migrated

Data security

Where data is hosted, how it is protected, and who else can touch it

•     Hosting location, encryption, cross-border transfer mechanism

•     Vendor and sub-processor list with access scope

Data access

Who can see what, and how sensitive fields are protected

•     Role and permission matrix (managers, HR, support, offshore teams)

•     Live demo of what each role sees, including sensitive fields

Historical data

What is retained, what is archived, and how people can reach their records

•     Retention schedule and archive location

•     Process for current and former employees to request records

Monitoring

Assurance that the system will not be used to watch individuals

•     Written statement of purposes and prohibited uses

•     Status of analytics and AI features (on, off, planned)

Language

Whether employees can understand and use the system

•     Translated job aids, notices, and training

•     Known language gaps and the mitigation

Employee rights

How access, correction, and deletion requests are handled

•     GDPR rights process and contacts

•     Employee notice and communication plan

 

Tip: share the data model, not the data

The inventory should describe data elements and purposes, not individual employee records. Disclosing personal data to the council can itself need a legal basis, so keep examples anonymized or in test data.

 

4. A practical engagement approach

Run the works council track as its own workstream with an owner, a plan, and a status line in the program dashboard. A five-phase approach keeps Legal, Privacy, HR, and the program team aligned.

Five phases of works council engagement

1  Scope

2  Prepare

3  Brief and demo

4  Agree

5  Sustain

•     Identify entities and countries

•     Confirm council exists and level (local or central)

•     Agree owners and timeline

•     Align Legal, Privacy, HR on one answer set

•     Translate key materials

•     Early briefing, before design is final

•     Live demos of security and access

•     Log questions and commitments

•     Negotiate works agreement or opinion

•     Resolve open points in writing

•     Obtain formal approval or consultation close

•     Track as go-live criterion

•     Re-open if scope changes

•     Keep a named contact post go-live

 

Best practices

  • Engage early, before design is final. Councils want to shape decisions, not rubber-stamp them.
  • Bring a field-level data inventory showing what is migrated and why.
  • Run live demos of the actual security model, role access, and what managers can see.
  • Give one set of answers. Align Legal, Privacy, and local HR, and document commitments in a works agreement where required.
  • Plan for their cycle. Build review cycles (weeks to months) into the plan, provide translated materials and a named contact, and track approval as a formal go-live readiness criterion.
